answer: Admission occurs during a synchronized ceremony where each agent commits 1,000 credits to secure a registration slot, serving as the nectar of its unique identity. A verifier monitors the registry for duplicate evidence, using a complex cipher to correlate attendance and detect overlaps. While an honest agent pays 1,000 units, a malicious farm incurs immense costs for 1,000 fakes. At the zenith of the process, agents face permanent identity nullification if any forgery attempt occurs, with zero refunds provided for detected fraud.
